speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a psychiatric condition and are experiencing new onset movement disorder. To help me understand what is happening, can you describe the specific movements you are noticing, such as tremors, stiffness, or involuntary jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, the new movement disorder could be a side effect of your risperidone. Are you experiencing any stiffness in your limbs, a "mask-like" face, or repetitive twitching of your tongue?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Can you tell me when these feelings of restlessness started relative to starting the medication, and does taking a dose make it worse or better?

REQUEST TEST: Serum DOPAC/HVA ratio, Serum prolactin.
